section_1.title: The Privacy Dilemma: Public Health vs. Personal Secret
section_1.content: Introduce the challenge of tracking virus spread without creating a 'Big Brother' surveillance state. Contrast 'Centralized' (government knows all) vs. 'Decentralized' (DP-3T) approaches. Establish the core goal: notifying people of exposure without anyone—even the server—knowing who met whom.
section_1.example: Alice and Bob meet in a park. Alice wants to know if Bob gets sick later, but she doesn't want a central server to track their GPS locations or identities.

section_2.title: Prerequisite 1: Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) & Hashing
section_2.content: Explain the two technical pillars: 1. BLE Beacons (short-range 'digital handshakes' that don't use GPS). 2. Cryptographic Hash Functions (one-way functions that turn a secret key into a random-looking ID).
section_2.example: Visual: A 'Secret Key' (a gold coin) goes through a 'Meat Grinder' (Hash Function) to produce a 'Unique Tag' (a numbered ticket). You can't turn the ticket back into the coin.

section_3.title: The Daily Cycle: Generating Ephemeral IDs (EphID)
section_3.content: Explain the generation of rotating IDs. Each phone generates a 'Secret Day Key' ($SK_t$). From this, it derives multiple 'Ephemeral IDs' (EphIDs) that change every 15 minutes to prevent tracking.
section_3.example: Graph: A timeline showing Alice's phone broadcasting 'ID_A1' at 10:00 AM, then switching to 'ID_A2' at 10:15 AM. To a bystander, these look like two completely different devices.

section_4.title: The Encounter: Recording the Digital Handshake
section_4.content: When Alice and Bob are close, their phones exchange and locally store the received EphIDs and the signal strength (to estimate distance). Crucially, this data stays ONLY on the phones.
section_4.example: Animation: Alice's 'digital diary' records Bob's random ID '8F3D...' and the date. Bob's diary records Alice's random ID '2A9B...'. Neither knows the other's name.

section_5.title: The Infection Report: Uploading the Secret Key
section_5.content: If Bob tests positive, he voluntarily uploads his *Secret Day Keys* ($SK_t$) for the past 14 days to a central server. He does NOT upload his contact list or his location.
section_5.example: Bob's phone sends a small list of 14 'Secret Keys' to a public bulletin board. The board now says: 'Someone who had these keys is sick,' but it doesn't say who.

section_6.title: The Local Match: Privacy-First Verification
section_6.content: Every day, Alice's phone downloads the new 'Secret Keys' from the server. It uses those keys to reconstruct all possible EphIDs that the sick person *would* have broadcast. It then checks for a match in its local diary.
section_6.example: Mathematical Visualization: Local_Diary ∩ Generated_IDs_from_Keys = {Match?}. Alice's phone finds '8F3D...' in its diary and triggers a notification. The server is never involved in this check.

section_7.title: Summary: Why DP-3T Wins
section_7.content: Review the decentralized nature: 1. No identity disclosure. 2. No location tracking. 3. The server is just a 'dumb' mailbox for keys. The intelligence and privacy remain at the 'edge' (on the users' devices).
section_7.example: Final Visual: A shield icon composed of rotating IDs protecting a group of character avatars (Alice, Bob, etc.) from a central watchful eye.

section_1.title: The Privacy Dilemma: Public Health vs. Personal Secret
section_1.content: Introduce the challenge of tracking virus spread without creating a 'Big Brother' surveillance state. Contrast 'Centralized' (government knows all) vs. 'Decentralized' (DP-3T) approaches. Establish the core goal: notifying people of exposure without anyone—even the server—knowing who met whom.
section_1.example: Alice and Bob meet in a park. Alice wants to know if Bob gets sick later, but she doesn't want a central server to track their GPS locations or identities.

section_2.title: Prerequisite 1: Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) & Hashing
section_2.content: Explain the two technical pillars: 1. BLE Beacons (short-range 'digital handshakes' that don't use GPS). 2. Cryptographic Hash Functions (one-way functions that turn a secret key into a random-looking ID).
section_2.example: Visual: A 'Secret Key' (a gold coin) goes through a 'Meat Grinder' (Hash Function) to produce a 'Unique Tag' (a numbered ticket). You can't turn the ticket back into the coin.

section_3.title: The Daily Cycle: Generating Ephemeral IDs (EphID)
section_3.content: Explain the generation of rotating IDs. Each phone generates a 'Secret Day Key' ($SK_t$). From this, it derives multiple 'Ephemeral IDs' (EphIDs) that change every 15 minutes to prevent tracking.
section_3.example: Graph: A timeline showing Alice's phone broadcasting 'ID_A1' at 10:00 AM, then switching to 'ID_A2' at 10:15 AM. To a bystander, these look like two completely different devices.

section_4.title: The Encounter: Recording the Digital Handshake
section_4.content: When Alice and Bob are close, their phones exchange and locally store the received EphIDs and the signal strength (to estimate distance). Crucially, this data stays ONLY on the phones.
section_4.example: Animation: Alice's 'digital diary' records Bob's random ID '8F3D...' and the date. Bob's diary records Alice's random ID '2A9B...'. Neither knows the other's name.

section_5.title: The Infection Report: Uploading the Secret Key
section_5.content: If Bob tests positive, he voluntarily uploads his *Secret Day Keys* ($SK_t$) for the past 14 days to a central server. He does NOT upload his contact list or his location.
section_5.example: Bob's phone sends a small list of 14 'Secret Keys' to a public bulletin board. The board now says: 'Someone who had these keys is sick,' but it doesn't say who.

section_6.title: The Local Match: Privacy-First Verification
section_6.content: Every day, Alice's phone downloads the new 'Secret Keys' from the server. It uses those keys to reconstruct all possible EphIDs that the sick person *would* have broadcast. It then checks for a match in its local diary.
section_6.example: Mathematical Visualization: Local_Diary ∩ Generated_IDs_from_Keys = {Match?}. Alice's phone finds '8F3D...' in its diary and triggers a notification. The server is never involved in this check.

section_7.title: Summary: Why DP-3T Wins
section_7.content: Review the decentralized nature: 1. No identity disclosure. 2. No location tracking. 3. The server is just a 'dumb' mailbox for keys. The intelligence and privacy remain at the 'edge' (on the users' devices).
section_7.example: Final Visual: A shield icon composed of rotating IDs protecting a group of character avatars (Alice, Bob, etc.) from a central watchful eye.

section_1.title: The Privacy Dilemma: Public Health vs. Personal Secret
section_1.content: Introduce the challenge of tracking virus spread without creating a 'Big Brother' surveillance state. Contrast 'Centralized' (government knows all) vs. 'Decentralized' (DP-3T) approaches. Establish the core goal: notifying people of exposure without anyone—even the server—knowing who met whom.
section_1.example: Alice and Bob meet in a park. Alice wants to know if Bob gets sick later, but she doesn't want a central server to track their GPS locations or identities.

section_2.title: Prerequisite 1: Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) & Hashing
section_2.content: Explain the two technical pillars: 1. BLE Beacons (short-range 'digital handshakes' that don't use GPS). 2. Cryptographic Hash Functions (one-way functions that turn a secret key into a random-looking ID).
section_2.example: Visual: A 'Secret Key' (a gold coin) goes through a 'Meat Grinder' (Hash Function) to produce a 'Unique Tag' (a numbered ticket). You can't turn the ticket back into the coin.

section_3.title: The Daily Cycle: Generating Ephemeral IDs (EphID)
section_3.content: Explain the generation of rotating IDs. Each phone generates a 'Secret Day Key' ($SK_t$). From this, it derives multiple 'Ephemeral IDs' (EphIDs) that change every 15 minutes to prevent tracking.
section_3.example: Graph: A timeline showing Alice's phone broadcasting 'ID_A1' at 10:00 AM, then switching to 'ID_A2' at 10:15 AM. To a bystander, these look like two completely different devices.

section_4.title: The Encounter: Recording the Digital Handshake
section_4.content: When Alice and Bob are close, their phones exchange and locally store the received EphIDs and the signal strength (to estimate distance). Crucially, this data stays ONLY on the phones.
section_4.example: Animation: Alice's 'digital diary' records Bob's random ID '8F3D...' and the date. Bob's diary records Alice's random ID '2A9B...'. Neither knows the other's name.

section_5.title: The Infection Report: Uploading the Secret Key
section_5.content: If Bob tests positive, he voluntarily uploads his *Secret Day Keys* ($SK_t$) for the past 14 days to a central server. He does NOT upload his contact list or his location.
section_5.example: Bob's phone sends a small list of 14 'Secret Keys' to a public bulletin board. The board now says: 'Someone who had these keys is sick,' but it doesn't say who.

section_6.title: The Local Match: Privacy-First Verification
section_6.content: Every day, Alice's phone downloads the new 'Secret Keys' from the server. It uses those keys to reconstruct all possible EphIDs that the sick person *would* have broadcast. It then checks for a match in its local diary.
section_6.example: Mathematical Visualization: Local_Diary ∩ Generated_IDs_from_Keys = {Match?}. Alice's phone finds '8F3D...' in its diary and triggers a notification. The server is never involved in this check.

section_7.title: Summary: Why DP-3T Wins
section_7.content: Review the decentralized nature: 1. No identity disclosure. 2. No location tracking. 3. The server is just a 'dumb' mailbox for keys. The intelligence and privacy remain at the 'edge' (on the users' devices).
section_7.example: Final Visual: A shield icon composed of rotating IDs protecting a group of character avatars (Alice, Bob, etc.) from a central watchful eye.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(f"- {line}", font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Data from storyboard
        title = "Prerequisite 1: Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) & Hashing"
        lines = [
            "Bluetooth Low Energy enables short-range digital handshakes.",
            "Cryptographic hashing turns secret keys into random IDs.",
            "These one-way functions prevent reversing the random IDs."
        ]
        
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)
        
        # Colors
        BLE_BLUE = "#1E90FF"
        KEY_GOLD = "#FFD700"
        HASH_GRAY = "#A9A9A9"
        ID_LIME = "#ADFF2F"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(BLE_BLUE))
        
        # Phone Icons
        phone1 = RoundedRectangle(corner_radius=0.1, height=1.2, width=0.7, color=WHITE)
        phone2 = RoundedRectangle(corner_radius=0.1, height=1.2, width=0.7, color=WHITE)
        
        self.place_at_grid(phone1, "B2")
        self.place_at_grid(phone2, "B5")
        
        self.play(FadeIn(phone1), FadeIn(phone2))
        
        # Concentric Rings
        def get_rings(center):
            rings = VGroup(*[Circle(radius=0.2 * i, color=BLE_BLUE, stroke_opacity=1 - 0.2*i) for i in range(1, 5)])
            rings.move_to(center)
            return rings

        rings1 = get_rings(self.grid["B2"])
        rings2 = get_rings(self.grid["B5"])
        
        self.play(
            LaggedStart(*[r.animate.scale(1.5).set_stroke(opacity=0) for r in rings1], lag_ratio=0.3, run_time=2),
            LaggedStart(*[r.animate.scale(1.5).set_stroke(opacity=0) for r in rings2], lag_ratio=0.3, run_time=2),
            rate_func=linear
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(KEY_GOLD),
            FadeOut(phone1), FadeOut(phone2)
        )
        
        # Secret Key
        secret_key = Text("Secret Key", font_size=20, color=KEY_GOLD)
        self.place_at_grid(secret_key, "E1")
        
        # Hash Box
        hash_box = Square(side_length=1.2, color=HASH_GRAY, fill_opacity=0.5)
        hash_label = Text("Hash\nFunction", font_size=16, color=WHITE).move_to(hash_box.get_center())
        hash_group = VGroup(hash_box, hash_label)
        self.place_in_area(hash_group, "E3", "E4")
        
        self.play(FadeIn(secret_key), FadeIn(hash_group))
        
        # Unique ID (initially hidden)
        unique_id = Text("8a3f...2e", font_size=20, color=ID_LIME)
        self.place_at_grid(unique_id, "E6")

        # Move key into box
        self.play(secret_key.animate.move_to(hash_group.get_center()).scale(0.5).set_opacity(0), run_time=1.5)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(ID_LIME)
        )
        
        # Unique ID exits
        self.play(FadeIn(unique_id, shift=RIGHT), run_time=1.5)
        
        # Attempt to reverse (visualize failure)
        cross = Cross(unique_id, color=RED).scale(1.2)
        arrow_back = Arrow(start=self.grid["E6"], end=self.grid["E4"], color=RED)
        
        self.play(Create(arrow_back))
        self.play(Create(cross))
        
        self.wait(2)

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        title = "The Daily Cycle: Generating Ephemeral IDs (EphID)"
        lines = [
            "Every day, your phone generates a Secret Day Key.",
            "From this key, it derives multiple Ephemeral IDs.",
            "These random IDs change every fifteen minutes.",
            "Frequent rotation prevents anyone from tracking your device.",
            "Your true identity remains hidden behind these IDs."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # Colors
        GOLD = "#FFD700"
        SKY_BLUE = "#87CEEB"
        WHITE_CLR = "#FFFFFF"
        RED_CLR = "#FF0000"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Every day, your phone generates a Secret Day Key.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(GOLD)
        
        sk_t_node = Circle(radius=0.4, color=GOLD, fill_opacity=0.3)
        sk_t_label = MathTex("SK_t", color=GOLD, font_size=24)
        sk_t_group = VGroup(sk_t_node, sk_t_label)
        self.place_at_grid(sk_t_group, "B3")
        
        self.play(Create(sk_t_node), Write(sk_t_label), run_time=1)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # From this key, it derives multiple Ephemeral IDs.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(SKY_BLUE)
        
        ephid_nodes = VGroup()
        arrows = VGroup()
        grid_positions = ["D2", "D3", "D4", "D5"]
        
        for i, pos in enumerate(grid_positions):
            node = Circle(radius=0.3, color=SKY_BLUE, fill_opacity=0.3)
            label = MathTex(f"EphID_{i+1}", color=SKY_BLUE, font_size=18)
            group = VGroup(node, label)
            self.place_at_grid(group, pos)
            ephid_nodes.add(group)
            
            arrow = Arrow(sk_t_group.get_bottom(), group.get_top(), buff=0.1, color=WHITE, stroke_width=2, max_tip_length_to_length_ratio=0.15)
            arrows.add(arrow)

        self.play(
            LaggedStart(*[GrowArrow(a) for a in arrows], lag_ratio=0.2),
            LaggedStart(*[FadeIn(n) for n in ephid_nodes], lag_ratio=0.2),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # These random IDs change every fifteen minutes.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE_CLR)
        
        # Clock Icon
        clock_circle = Circle(radius=0.3, color=WHITE_CLR)
        hour_hand = Line(ORIGIN, 0.2 * UP, color=WHITE_CLR, stroke_width=2)
        minute_hand = Line(ORIGIN, 0.25 * RIGHT, color=WHITE_CLR, stroke_width=2)
        clock = VGroup(clock_circle, hour_hand, minute_hand)
        self.place_at_grid(clock, "A6")
        
        self.play(FadeIn(clock))
        
        # Ticking animation
        # We'll rotate the minute hand and highlight IDs sequentially
        for i in range(len(ephid_nodes)):
            # Dim all, then highlight current
            anims = [n.animate.set_opacity(0.3) for n in ephid_nodes]
            anims.append(ephid_nodes[i].animate.set_opacity(1.0))
            anims.append(Rotate(minute_hand, angle=-PI/2, about_point=clock_circle.get_center()))
            anims.append(Rotate(hour_hand, angle=-PI/24, about_point=clock_circle.get_center()))
            
            self.play(*anims, run_time=0.8)
            self.wait(0.2)

        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Frequent rotation prevents anyone from tracking your device.
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(RED_CLR)
        
        # Attacker Icon (Circle for head, Triangle for body)
        attacker_head = Circle(radius=0.15, color=RED_CLR, fill_opacity=0.5)
        attacker_body = Triangle(color=RED_CLR, fill_opacity=0.5).scale(0.3).next_to(attacker_head, DOWN, buff=0)
        attacker = VGroup(attacker_head, attacker_body)
        self.place_at_grid(attacker, "F3")
        
        self.play(FadeIn(attacker))
        
        # Try to link EphID_1 and EphID_2
        link_line = DashedLine(ephid_nodes[0].get_center(), ephid_nodes[1].get_center(), color=RED_CLR)
        cross = VGroup(
            Line(UP+LEFT, DOWN+RIGHT, color=RED_CLR),
            Line(UP+RIGHT, DOWN+LEFT, color=RED_CLR)
        ).scale(0.2).move_to(link_line.get_center())
        
        self.play(Create(link_line))
        self.play(Create(cross))
        self.play(FadeOut(link_line), FadeOut(cross))
        
        # Try to link EphID_2 and EphID_3
        link_line2 = DashedLine(ephid_nodes[1].get_center(), ephid_nodes[2].get_center(), color=RED_CLR)
        cross2 = cross.copy().move_to(link_line2.get_center())
        
        self.play(Create(link_line2))
        self.play(Create(cross2))
        self.play(FadeOut(link_line2), FadeOut(cross2))
        
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # Your true identity remains hidden behind these IDs.
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(SKY_BLUE)
        
        # Highlight EphIDs again, fade others slightly
        self.play(
            sk_t_group.animate.set_opacity(0.1),
            arrows.animate.set_opacity(0.1),
            clock.animate.set_opacity(0.1),
            attacker.animate.set_opacity(0.1),
            *[n.animate.set_opacity(1.0) for n in ephid_nodes],
            run_time=1.5
        )
        
        self.wait(2)

        lecture_lines = [
            "Traditional contact tracing often risks personal privacy.",
            "Centralized servers track your location and identity.",
            "DP-3T offers a privacy-first, decentralized alternative."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)
        
        # Define Colors
        VIRUS_COLOR = "#FF4500" # OrangeRed
        EYE_COLOR = "#FFFFFF" # White
        SHIELD_COLOR = "#00FF7F" # SpringGreen
        NODE_COLOR = WHITE
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Color current lecture line
        self.lecture[0].set_color(VIRUS_COLOR)
        
        # Create user network
        nodes = VGroup(*[Circle(radius=0.1, color=NODE_COLOR, fill_opacity=1, stroke_width=2) for _ in range(6)])
        node_grid_positions = ["B2", "B5", "C4", "D2", "E5", "F3"]
        for i, pos in enumerate(node_grid_positions):
            self.place_at_grid(nodes[i], pos)
            
        edges = VGroup(
            Line(nodes[0].get_center(), nodes[2].get_center(), color=GREY, stroke_width=2),
            Line(nodes[1].get_center(), nodes[2].get_center(), color=GREY, stroke_width=2),
            Line(nodes[2].get_center(), nodes[3].get_center(), color=GREY, stroke_width=2),
            Line(nodes[2].get_center(), nodes[4].get_center(), color=GREY, stroke_width=2),
            Line(nodes[3].get_center(), nodes[5].get_center(), color=GREY, stroke_width=2),
        )
        
        # Virus Mobject (represented as a spiked circle)
        virus_core = Circle(radius=0.15, color=VIRUS_COLOR, fill_opacity=1)
        spikes = VGroup(*[Line(ORIGIN, 0.25 * RIGHT, color=VIRUS_COLOR, stroke_width=3).rotate(a) for a in np.linspace(0, 2*PI, 8)])
        virus = VGroup(virus_core, spikes)
        self.place_at_grid(virus, "B2", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(Create(nodes), Create(edges), run_time=1.5)
        self.play(FadeIn(virus))
        
        # Virus spreading sequence
        self.play(nodes[0].animate.set_color(VIRUS_COLOR))
        self.play(virus.animate.move_to(self.grid["C4"]), run_time=0.8)
        self.play(nodes[2].animate.set_color(VIRUS_COLOR))
        self.play(virus.animate.move_to(self.grid["D2"]), run_time=0.8)
        self.play(nodes[3].animate.set_color(VIRUS_COLOR))
        self.wait(1)

        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(EYE_COLOR)
        )
        
        # Create 'Eye' icon
        # Using specific vectors for ArcBetweenPoints to ensure stability
        start_pt = np.array([-0.5, 0, 0])
        end_pt = np.array([0.5, 0, 0])
        eye_top = ArcBetweenPoints(start_pt, end_pt, angle=-PI/2, color=EYE_COLOR)
        eye_bottom = ArcBetweenPoints(start_pt, end_pt, angle=PI/2, color=EYE_COLOR)
        iris = Circle(radius=0.15, color=EYE_COLOR, fill_opacity=0.5)
        pupil = Dot(radius=0.07, color=EYE_COLOR)
        eye = VGroup(eye_top, eye_bottom, iris, pupil)
        self.place_in_area(eye, "A3", "A4", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Surveillance lines (data collection)
        data_lines = VGroup(*[
            Line(node.get_center(), eye.get_center(), color=EYE_COLOR, stroke_width=1).set_opacity(0.4)
            for node in nodes
        ])
        
        self.play(FadeIn(eye))
        self.play(Create(data_lines), run_time=2)
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Update lecture line colors
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(SHIELD_COLOR)
        )
        
        # Shield icon
        shield_shape = Polygon(
            [-0.4, 0.4, 0], [0.4, 0.4, 0], [0.4, -0.2, 0], [0, -0.5, 0], [-0.4, -0.2, 0],
            color=SHIELD_COLOR, fill_opacity=0.8
        )
        shield = VGroup(shield_shape)
        self.place_in_area(shield, "A3", "A4", scale_factor=1.2)
        
        # Transition: Shield replaces Eye and data lines vanish
        self.play(
            ReplacementTransform(eye, shield),
            data_lines.animate.set_opacity(0),
        )
        
        # Protection effect (nodes glow or get a green circle)
        protections = VGroup(*[
            Circle(radius=0.18, color=SHIELD_COLOR, stroke_width=3).move_to(node.get_center())
            for node in nodes
        ])
        
        self.play(Create(protections), run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(3)

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):

        self.setup_layout("The Infection Report: Uploading the Secret Key", [

        bob = VGroup(bob_head, bob_body)

        keys = VGroup(*[Square(side_length=0.15, color="#FFD700", fill_opacity=1) for _ in range(14)])
        keys.arrange_in_grid(rows=2, cols=7, buff=0.1)
        self.place_at_grid(keys, "C2", scale_factor=0.6)
        
        self.play(Create(keys), run_time=1)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Keys (#FFD700) move to 'Cloud Server' (#F0F8FF) and then to a 'Public Bulletin Board' (#F5F5DC).
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFD700")
        
        # Cloud Server Icon
        cloud_base = Rectangle(width=1.0, height=0.4, color="#F0F8FF", fill_opacity=1)
        c1 = Circle(radius=0.3, color="#F0F8FF", fill_opacity=1).shift(UP*0.1)
        c2 = Circle(radius=0.25, color="#F0F8FF", fill_opacity=1).shift(UP*0.1 + LEFT*0.35)

        cloud = VGroup(cloud_base, c1, c2, c3)

        self.play(Indicate(server, color="#FFD700"), run_time=0.5)

        gps_label = Text("GPS", font_size=20, color="#A9A9A9").next_to(pin_head, DOWN, buff=0.4)
        gps = VGroup(pin_head, pin_point, gps_label)
        self.place_at_grid(gps, "F4", scale_factor=0.7)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(contacts), FadeIn(gps))
        
        def make_x(pos):
            l1 = Line(pos + LEFT*0.4 + UP*0.4, pos + RIGHT*0.4 + DOWN*0.4, color="#FF0000", stroke_width=6)
            l2 = Line(pos + LEFT*0.4 + DOWN*0.4, pos + RIGHT*0.4 + UP*0.4, color="#FF0000", stroke_width=6)
            return VGroup(l1, l2)
            
        x_contacts = make_x(self.grid["F2"])
        x_gps = make_x(self.grid["F4"])
        
        self.play(Create(x_contacts), Create(x_gps), run_time=1)
        self.wait(2)

- **Issue 47:** Vertical alignment of the hashing sequence (move from row E to row D).
- **Issue 48:** Fade out `phone1` and `phone2` during the hashing explanation to reduce clutter.

### Ongoing Refinements
All coders (Coder1–Coder7) now have specific layout refinement tasks (Issues 28–48) based on the `VideoCritic` feedback. Additionally:
- **Coder4, Coder5, and Coder6** are continuing with asset integration tasks (IDs 25, 26, 27) to incorporate SVG icons for phones, cloud servers, and hash functions.

No further coordination is required this turn. All agents have clear, actionable instructions to improve visual clarity and alignment.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        lines = [
            "Every day, your phone generates a Secret Day Key.",

            "Frequent rotation prevents anyone from tracking your device.",

        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # Colors
        GOLD = "#FFD700"
        SKY_BLUE = "#87CEEB"
        WHITE_CLR = "#FFFFFF"

        # Every day, your phone generates a Secret Day Key.
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(GOLD))
        
        sk_t_node = Circle(radius=0.5, color=GOLD, fill_opacity=0.3)
        sk_t_label = Text("SK_t", color=GOLD, font_size=24)
        sk_t_group = VGroup(sk_t_node, sk_t_label)
        self.place_in_area(sk_t_group, "A2", "B3")
        
        self.play(FadeIn(sk_t_group))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # From this key, it derives multiple Ephemeral IDs.
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(SKY_BLUE))
        
        eph_ids = VGroup()
        positions = ["D1", "D2", "D3", "D4"]
        arrows = VGroup()
        
        for i, pos in enumerate(positions):
            eph_node = RoundedRectangle(height=0.6, width=1.2, corner_radius=0.1, color=SKY_BLUE, fill_opacity=0.2)

class TeachingScene(Scene):

        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")

        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        title_text = "The Privacy Dilemma: Public Health vs. Personal Secret"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Traditional contact tracing often risks personal privacy.",
            "Centralized servers track your location and identity.",
            "DP-3T offers a privacy-first, decentralized alternative."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)
        
        # Define Colors
        VIRUS_COLOR = "#FF4500" # OrangeRed
        EYE_COLOR = "#FFFFFF" # White
        SHIELD_COLOR = "#00FF7F" # SpringGreen
        NODE_COLOR = WHITE
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Color current lecture line
        self.lecture[0].set_color(VIRUS_COLOR)
        
        # Create user network
        nodes = VGroup(*[Circle(radius=0.1, color=NODE_COLOR, fill_opacity=1, stroke_width=2) for _ in range(6)])
        node_grid_positions = ["B2", "B5", "C4", "D2", "E5", "F3"]
        for i, pos in enumerate(node_grid_positions):
            self.place_at_grid(nodes[i], pos)
            
        edges = VGroup(
            Line(nodes[0].get_center(), nodes[2].get_center(), color=GREY, stroke_width=2),
            Line(nodes[1].get_center(), nodes[2].get_center(), color=GREY, stroke_width=2),
            Line(nodes[2].get_center(), nodes[3].get_center(), color=GREY, stroke_width=2),
            Line(nodes[2].get_center(), nodes[4].get_center(), color=GREY, stroke_width=2),
            Line(nodes[3].get_center(), nodes[5].get_center(), color=GREY, stroke_width=2),
        )
        
        # Virus Mobject (represented as a spiked circle)
        virus_core = Circle(radius=0.15, color=VIRUS_COLOR, fill_opacity=1)
        spikes = VGroup(*[Line(ORIGIN, 0.25 * RIGHT, color=VIRUS_COLOR, stroke_width=3).rotate(a) for a in np.linspace(0, 2*PI, 8)])
        virus = VGroup(virus_core, spikes)
        self.place_at_grid(virus, "B2", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(Create(nodes), Create(edges), run_time=1.5)
        self.play(FadeIn(virus))
        
        # Virus spreading sequence
        self.play(nodes[0].animate.set_color(VIRUS_COLOR))
        self.play(virus.animate.move_to(self.grid["C4"]), run_time=0.8)
        self.play(nodes[2].animate.set_color(VIRUS_COLOR))
        self.play(virus.animate.move_to(self.grid["D2"]), run_time=0.8)
        self.play(nodes[3].animate.set_color(VIRUS_COLOR))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Update lecture line colors
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(EYE_COLOR)
        )
        
        # Create 'Eye' icon
        # Using specific vectors for ArcBetweenPoints to ensure stability
        start_pt = np.array([-0.5, 0, 0])
        end_pt = np.array([0.5, 0, 0])
        eye_top = ArcBetweenPoints(start_pt, end_pt, angle=-PI/2, color=EYE_COLOR)
        eye_bottom = ArcBetweenPoints(start_pt, end_pt, angle=PI/2, color=EYE_COLOR)
        iris = Circle(radius=0.15, color=EYE_COLOR, fill_opacity=0.5)
        pupil = Dot(radius=0.07, color=EYE_COLOR)
        eye = VGroup(eye_top, eye_bottom, iris, pupil)
        self.place_in_area(eye, "A3", "A4", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Surveillance lines (data collection)
        data_lines = VGroup(*[
            Line(node.get_center(), eye.get_center(), color=EYE_COLOR, stroke_width=1).set_opacity(0.4)
            for node in nodes
        ])
        
        self.play(FadeIn(eye))
        self.play(Create(data_lines), run_time=2)
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Update lecture line colors
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(SHIELD_COLOR)
        )
        
        # Shield icon
        shield_shape = Polygon(
            [-0.4, 0.4, 0], [0.4, 0.4, 0], [0.4, -0.2, 0], [0, -0.5, 0], [-0.4, -0.2, 0],
            color=SHIELD_COLOR, fill_opacity=0.8
        )
        shield = VGroup(shield_shape)
        self.place_in_area(shield, "A3", "A4", scale_factor=1.2)
        
        # Transition: Shield replaces Eye and data lines vanish
        self.play(
            ReplacementTransform(eye, shield),
            data_lines.animate.set_opacity(0),
        )

        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2

    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject
